newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares fall sharply on fresh selling.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares fall sharply on fresh selling.

text.p: Calcutta shares ended sharply lower on Thursday on fresh selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
They said yesterday's price rise was curbed as speculators who covered their short positions earlier were back in the ring taking new short positions at higher levels.
The Calcutta closing sensex was not immedietely available.

"FIIs are selling at each rise in prices and their total purchases are very low in terms of volumes. The short covering surfaced since the Bombay bourse was closed on Monday and Tuesday for Hindu festivals. But the very same speculators are again selling blue-chips," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.
"The technicals of the market are very weak and there is no investment buying in sight. Sporadic rises in prices will not sustain for long," Sharma added.
